entries.title: Player AI Assistant: your own companion
q: what is the player ai assistant
a helper that plays like a player
entries.answer: Your Player AI Assistant is a companion of your own: it talks with you, takes orders in plain words or by voice, and plays like a player.
more: It chops, mines, farms, crafts the whole chain, smelts, builds the mod's buildings, fights, fetches and tidies, and grows better with use.
It belongs to you alone: it is not one of the village folk, takes no town job and draws no wage.
It never fights people: a knock from you does it no harm, and it only ever fights monsters.
steps: Press Y (or right-click your assistant) to open its panel.
Type what you want in the Talk tab, click an order, or hold Z and say it.
tips: Ask it "what can you do?" for a list, or "what are you doing?" any time.

entries.title: Getting your Player AI Assistant
q: how do i get an ai assistant
how do i get my assistant
how do i get a player ai assistant
how do i make an assistant
entries.answer: Press Y and click Get my assistant: the first one is free. Or craft an Assistant Whistle, or place an Assistant Spawner and click it.
more: Assistant Whistle: 4 iron ingots in the corners, 4 redstone on the sides, a gold ingot in the middle. Use it on the ground and your assistant appears there; blown later, it calls your assistant to you at once.

Assistant Spawner: 8 rotten flesh round a diamond. Place it and click it: your assistant comes out, and the spawner is its home and the place it comes back to if it falls. A sneak-click on the spawner hires a crew hand instead.
However it appears, it is yours for good: it shows your name, obeys only you (and operators), and follows you through logouts and into other dimensions.
Each player may have one (the server's operator can allow more). At the limit you are told to dismiss the one you have first.
steps: Press Y: with no assistant yet, the panel offers one.
Click Get my assistant.
It says hello and offers a short tour.
tips: The U page has a Player AI Assistant button too.

entries.title: Talking to your assistant
q: how do i talk to my assistant
how do i give my assistant orders
what can i say to my assistant
tell the assistant what to do
entries.answer: Open its panel (Y) and type in the Talk tab as you would to a person; it answers in words, aloud, and in a bubble over its head.
more: It reads typos and slang, and chains steps: "chop 64 logs, then make planks and sticks, then build a crafting table by my house".
"Here", "there" and "that" mean what you are looking at: look at a chest and say "put everything in that chest".
Before a long or big job it checks with you (OK, Change, Cancel). "Stop" and "undo" always work at once.
Ask it about the mod too ("how do I start a business?"): it answers from the Guide.
When it isn't sure what you mean, it asks back with choices to click: it never just ignores you.
steps: Press Y.
Type an order such as "get me 16 logs" and press Enter, or click one of the suggestions under the box.
tips: The suggestions change with what you look at and hold, and the time of day.
No chat is used: everything is in its own panel.

entries.title: The assistant's Orders tab
q: make my assistant build a house
how do i make my assistant follow me
entries.answer: The Orders tab has a button for each common job; the ones with choices ask how many and where, then send the order.
more: Follow, Stay, Come, Guard me, Guard here, Gather wood or stone, Mine ore, Mine down, Farm, Build, Craft, Smelt, Deposit, Fight, Bring food, Light up, Sort chests, Go home, Stop.
It gets what a job needs first, as a player would: a pickaxe before stone, the blocks and the furniture before a house, a hoe and seeds before a field.
steps: Press Y and open Orders.
Click an order; pick the amount and the place if it asks.
Click Go: its answer shows in Talk.
controls: [Come here key, unset at first] call it to you (set it in Controls)
tips: Building uses the same drawings and builder as the towns, so its houses look as good.

entries.title: The assistant's action wheel (X)
q: tell the assistant to mine this
entries.answer: Look at something and press X: the wheel offers what fits it first (mine this vein, use that chest, attack that, farm this field, build there).
more: Click a choice, or hold X, point and let go. The everyday orders (come, follow, guard, stay, stop) are round the rest of it.
steps: Look at a block, a chest or a creature.
Press X and pick what your assistant should do with it.

entries.title: What your assistant is doing (Jobs)
entries.answer: The Jobs tab lists what it is doing now and next, with progress and a time; move any up or down, cancel it, or pause them all.
more: A small line at the top left of the screen shows what it is doing too ("Chopping logs 12/16"); switch it off in Settings.
When it can't do something it says why and offers a fix to click ("I need a pickaxe: make one?").
Small snags it sorts out itself, as a player would: it makes a new pickaxe when one wears out, climbs out of a pit it dug, and walks to the nearest trees it can see when none are close.
steps: Press Y and open Jobs.
Use the arrows to reorder, the cross to cancel, Pause to hold the list.
tips: Say "stop" to stop everything at once, or "undo" to take back your last order.

entries.title: Talking to your assistant by voice
q: how do i talk to my assistant with my voice
entries.answer: Turn on Listen in your assistant's Settings tab, then hold Z and speak: your words go to it like a typed order.
more: On Windows it uses Windows' own offline speech recognition. Elsewhere (or if that's missing) it asks to download a small offline speech model (about 40 MB, once) into your config folder.
It speaks its replies with your computer's own voice: pick the voice, speed and volume in Settings, or switch speaking off. Its words always show as well.
Only the recognised words go to the server: no sound leaves your computer.

Accent: English (UK), English (US) or Auto in Settings. On Windows it uses the UK recogniser when installed. The offline model is US English (there is no small British one), so it listens for its own phrases, which copes well with a British accent.
steps: Press Y, open Settings and switch Listen on (agree to the download if it asks).
Close the panel, hold Z, say "follow me", let go.
tips: A light and your words as they are heard show above the hotbar while you hold the key.

entries.title: Auto-help: your assistant on its own
q: what does my assistant do on its own
stop my assistant doing things on its own
entries.answer: With nothing to do and auto-help on, it does useful things for you and says what and why; click Don't do that to veto one.
more: It steps in when something hostile comes at you, puts a full pack away, keeps a cold furnace fuelled, picks ripe crops, brings you food if you have none, lights dark ground at night, and now and then sorts the chests at home.
Switch it off in Settings, or say "only do what I say".
steps: Press Y, open Settings, and set Auto-help on or off.
tips: Anything you ask comes first: it drops what it chose to do.

entries.title: Your assistant's panel
entries.answer: Press Y or right-click it: Talk, Orders, Jobs, Pack (its things and gear), Stats (level and record) and Settings (every setting, in sections down the left).
more: Chattiness: Quiet, Low, Normal or Chatty (it always answers you). Ask before big jobs, may use your chests, may break blocks near your builds, shelter at night, how far it roams, and how much it may spend at a market for you.

Pack shows it in 3D with its gear slots, its pack (two rows to start, the third at level 3) and your inventory: drag things either way, or click to hand over. Equip best, Give me everything, Dump (the junk), Sort, and Keep (locks on what it should hang on to).

Settings sections: Personality (the triangle, name), Voice, Behaviour (auto-help, chests, roaming, chattiness, jokes, language), Look (its outfit, this panel's size, high contrast, subtitles), Keys (talk mode, every key, pings) and Advanced (reset, its bed and home, dismiss).
The panel opens on the tab you had last.
Personalities: Cheerful, Dry or Calm. Looks: eight outfits.
steps: Press Y and open Settings.
Pick a section on the left, then click a setting to change it.
tips: Replay the tour from Settings, Advanced any time.

entries.title: If your assistant falls, or is far away
q: assistant didnt follow me to the nether
entries.answer: A fallen assistant comes back after a minute, at its spawner or beside you, keeping its pack. A whistle brings it back at once.
more: It leaves with you when you log out and is beside you when you're back; it follows you through portals unless it is busy or told to stay.
Far away or lost in an unloaded place? The summon button in its panel, or a blown whistle, calls it to you.
steps: Press Y: the panel says when it will be back.
Or use an Assistant Whistle: no waiting.
tips: It gets itself out of trouble too: stuck, in lava or drowning, it comes back to you.

entries.title: Your assistant is yours, not a villager
q: does my assistant count as folk
will the town hire my assistant
difference between my assistant and the folk
can my assistant join a town
entries.answer: Your assistant is entirely separate from the village folk: it is never a citizen, takes no town job, home or wage, and works only for you.
more: Towns don't count it among their folk or hire it, and their guards treat it as your companion.
It respects other people's ground: it won't break, build or open chests on a town's ground or in someone else's land unless the server allows it.

entries.title: Troubleshooting your assistant's voice
entries.answer: Check Listen is on in Settings and the talk key is Z; the footer and the line above the hotbar say what's wrong. Typing always works.
more: "No microphone found": the game can't reach your microphone; check your system's privacy settings let Java use it.
No speech heard on Linux or macOS: turn Listen on and agree to the model download (it needs the internet once).
Silent replies: on Linux install espeak-ng; on Windows and macOS the system's own voice is used. Speaking can be switched on in Settings.
steps: Press Y, open Settings, look at the line under Listen and under Speak.

entries.title: Your assistant's personality (the triangle)
entries.answer: In Settings, Personality, drag the dot in the triangle: Serious at the top, Funny bottom left, Gloomy bottom right. Anywhere between mixes them.
more: Presets snap it: Professional, Banter, Joker, Doom and Balanced. A sample line shows what it'll sound like.
Chattiness sets how often it speaks unasked. At "Won't shut up" with the dot at Funny it becomes the Joke Machine: a remark on what you're doing every 10 to 20 seconds.
Warnings are always said plainly first. When you die it says where your things are and offers to fetch them.
Say "tell me a joke", or give it some lip; it answers in kind and still does the job.
steps: Press Y and open the Settings tab.
Drag the dot, or click a preset; set Chattiness underneath.
tips: Gloomy is comic pessimism about chores and weather; it still does every job properly.

entries.title: Make your assistant be quiet (or stop joking)
q: how do i make my assistant talk again
entries.answer: Tell it "shut up" (or click Quiet) and it only answers you and warns you. Tell it "no more jokes" and it talks plainly. "You can talk again" brings it back.
more: It understands most ways of saying it, typos too: be quiet, pipe down, zip it, give it a rest, put a sock in it, wind your neck in, button it.
Quiet still answers every order and still warns you about danger. It never sulks or works any worse.
It stays quiet, even after you log out, until you say "you can talk again" or "jokes back on". Its nameplate and the HUD say "quiet" or "no jokes" while it lasts.
Chattiness in Settings sets how often it talks unasked: about once every few minutes on Normal. Only Won't shut up keeps going.
steps: Press X for the action wheel and click Quiet, or say or type "shut up".
To let it talk again, click Talk again, or say "you can talk again".
controls: [Quiet key, unset at first] hush it or let it talk again (set it in Controls)
tips: Settings > Behaviour > Jokes cycles Talking, No jokes and Quiet.

entries.title: Your assistant matches your energy
q: why is my assistant rude back
can my assistant roast other players
entries.answer: Say it nicely and it's warm; bark it and it's dry; be rude and it fires back a witty roast. It still does the job straight away, every time.
more: Language in Settings sets how strong its comebacks get: Clean never swears (the default), Cheeky is mild (bloody, damn, arse), Unfiltered swears back. The server can cap it, and Settings says so.
It only roasts you when you started it, and only what you do in the game: dying a lot, hoarding dirt, bad builds, being bossy.

Other players can right-click it to chat. It answers them by name, in kind, and sticks up for you if they're rude about you. It never starts it, never takes their orders, and gets bored of anyone who keeps on.
Roast back (On, Only when insulted, Off) and Defend me are in Settings. Quiet or no jokes silences all of it.
steps: Press Y, open Settings, and set Language.
To answer someone else's assistant, right-click it and type, or click a quick line.
controls: Right-click someone else's assistant to chat
tips: A please or a thanks cools it down after a rude run.

entries.title: Choosing your assistant's look
entries.answer: Open the Look tab and click a look: 18 to choose from, including a skeleton, a zombie, a creeper hoodie and a tall enderman.
more: Changing is free and instant, and everyone sees it. Drag the preview to turn it round.
Each look brings a few remarks of its own, and some about itself, about one remark in five.
steps: Press Y and open the Look tab.
Click a look in the list.
tips: The skeleton is very aware it's built like a chopstick.

entries.title: Natural-sounding voices for your assistant
entries.answer: Its voice comes inside the mod: an expressive British voice that laughs, sighs and performs (on a fast computer), the natural Kokoro voices (on any computer), or your computer's own basic voice if you pick it.
more: Nothing is downloaded and nothing needs installing: the voices are in the mod jar and are unpacked into your game folder (mc_assistant-cache) once, the first time you have an assistant, each file checked.
Settings > Voice > Engine: Auto (the default) times your computer and picks the best voice it can keep up with; or choose Expressive, Natural or Basic yourself.

Expressive voices: Arthur and Callum (men), Harriet and Elsie (women), all British. Each look gets a fitting one: Callum for the pirate, the miner and the mobs, Elsie for the ranger, the farmer and the chef.
Natural voices (Kokoro): George, Lewis, Daniel, Fable, Emma, Isabella, Alice, Lily, and American ones.

Its personality is in the voice: a Funny one chuckles after a punchline, a Gloomy one sighs, a Daft sense of humour laughs out loud, a Sincere one gasps when you die, a Serious one says it straight. Expression in Settings turns that up or down (0: just the words). Never a sound on a warning.
Its voice comes from where it stands: quieter far away and from the left or right. Turn on Radio to hear it at full volume anywhere. The game's Voice/Speech slider sets its volume too.
Lines never talk over each other: one waits for the last to finish, a warning cuts in, and an old progress report is dropped when a newer one arrives.
steps: Press Y, open Settings, click Voice.
Choose an Engine, or leave it on Auto.
Press Test voice, or the play button beside a voice, to hear it.
tips: On a slow computer Auto keeps the natural voice, so the game never stutters for the sake of a laugh.

entries.title: Voices in a modpack: what's inside and the credits
entries.answer: Everything the voices need is inside the mod jar, all free to share: a modpack only has to include the mod and keep the credits below.
more: Chatterbox-Turbo (the expressive voice) by Resemble AI: MIT licence. Kokoro (the natural voice): Apache-2.0. misaki's pronouncing dictionaries: Apache-2.0. ONNX Runtime: MIT.

The expressive voices (Arthur, Callum, Harriet, Elsie) are made from the CSTR VCTK Corpus 0.92 (Centre for Speech Technology Research, University of Edinburgh), CC BY 4.0: speakers p226, p227, p228 and p225. Credit: "Voice references from the CSTR VCTK Corpus (University of Edinburgh), CC BY 4.0."

Pack makers can unpack ahead of time: start the game once with the pack's mods and the voices go to mc_assistant-cache/voice/ in the game folder, ready to ship in the pack. They are checked at every start and unpacked again if damaged.
A development build without voices inside takes an offline voice pack zip in config/ instead (tools/voice/build_voice_pack.py).
tips: Listening (speech recognition) is separate, off by default, and asks before fetching its model.

entries.title: Voice with a British (or other) accent
q: my assistant doesnt understand my accent
entries.answer: Set Accent to English (UK) in Settings. On Windows, add the UK English speech pack; then use short orders and keep your mic level steady.
more: Windows: Settings > Time & language > Speech, and add English (United Kingdom). The Settings tab says which recogniser is in use.
Train Windows to your voice: Control Panel > Speech Recognition > Train your computer to better understand you.
Short orders work best ("follow me", "get us 16 logs", "bung it in the chest"): they match its phrase list, which copes with any accent.
Speak at your usual pace with the mic close; the level light above the hotbar should move but not stay full.
With UK set it also speaks in a British voice if your computer has one (Hazel or George on Windows, Daniel or Kate on a Mac).
steps: Press Y and open the Settings tab; click Accent until it reads English (UK).
Read the line under Listen: it names the recogniser and how to add the UK one.
tips: Mis-hears like "lugs" for logs or "fallow" for follow are put right for spoken orders.

entries.title: Pinging orders
q: point at something for my assistant
tell my assistant to go there
entries.answer: Tap the middle mouse button on something to drop a "look here" marker; hold it for a wheel of what your assistant can do with it (chop that, mine the vein, attack that, go there).
more: A tap on its own is only a marker, for you and any friends near by: it never orders your assistant. It becomes an order when you pick from the wheel, tap it again, or say or type an order within five seconds (a ring round the marker counts down). "That" and "there" then mean the ping.
Talking works the same way: as you speak, what you look at is pinged, and each "that" means the next thing you looked at: "chop that, and that, then come back".
"Remember this spot as the mine", then later "go to the mine". It also knows "go back to where I died" and "go to my bed".
"Ping the nearest iron", "find me a tree", "where's the closest village": it looks in what's loaded round you and marks it.
"Cancel that ping", "clear all pings", "skip that one" and "do the tree first" change its list.
Pick "Mark an area" on the ground, then ping the other corner, for a wheel of things to do with the whole area (clear it, farm it, light it).
Markers have a colour and a shape for each kind (move: circle, attack: diamond, gather: square, danger: triangle, build: hexagon), so colour is never the only clue.
steps: Aim at a tree, then press and keep holding the ping button.
Point at "Chop that" and let go.
Or tap the middle button on it and say "chop that" within five seconds.
controls: [Middle mouse] tap: marker, hold: ping wheel
[Shift + ping] add a stop to a route (ping key off the middle button, or Ping only)
tips: The ping key, and whether the middle button pings or picks blocks, are in the panel's Settings, Keys.
Other players' pings never order your assistant.
"Act on quick pings" (off at first) makes a plain tap do the first option at once.

entries.title: Levelling up your assistant
q: how does my assistant level up
entries.answer: It earns experience from the work it does for you (more at harder difficulties) and climbs ten levels slowly: level 10 takes many game days.
more: Every level makes it better at what takes skill, and the Progress tab shows by how much: it digs, chops and plants at a real player's pace (break speed is a player's, by the tool in hand, at every level; a hand action about every 0.6 seconds), so levels buy planning instead: fewer idle gaps between actions, better routes, its reach from 4.5 blocks to 5.4, its reactions from 600 ms to 150 ms, harder hits and a steadier bow; its hearts grow from 10 (like a player) to 20 in two rows, and its pack's third row opens at level 3. Ores and gear open by level too (an operator can move a rung or switch the ladders off): coal ore at 2, copper ore and nether quartz at 3, iron ore at 4, gold ore, redstone ore and lapis ore at 5, diamond ore at 6, emerald ore and obsidian at 7, ancient debris at 8, spawners and budding amethyst (silk touch, when asked) at 9; the shield at 2, snowballs, eggs and the fishing rod at 3, armour up to iron at 4, the crossbow at 5, diamond gear and splash potions at 6, the trident and ender pearls at 7, firework rockets and the elytra at 8, the mace and netherite gear at 9.

Its bow is a real archer's, never an aimbot: it draws (both arms up, the bow bending), turns onto the target no faster than its level allows, judges the distance by eye, leads a moving target by what it saw a moment ago, and looses where it points, shaken by its hands. Hits at 30 blocks on a standing / a strafing mob: level 1 27% / 10%, level 4 49% / 16%, level 7 87% / 31%, level 10 99% / 49%. Its range grows from 16 to 43 blocks.
The Stats tab lists every level's numbers, and its own bow's record (arrows loosed and on target).

Each level opens new skills: bridging and taming (2), villager trading (3), shield blocks and leading shots (4), brewing and maps (5), enchanting, Nether trips and better gear (6), trick shots and parkour (7), the water-bucket clutch and elytra flying (8), ender pearls (9) and the End (10).
Ask for something it hasn't the level for and it says which level it needs.
A level gained comes with a chime, a cheer, a line in its own voice and a toast on your screen.
Operators can change how fast every assistant levels from Settings, Advanced.
steps: Press Y and open Stats.
Read "Next at L..." under its experience bar, and its skills list on the right.
tips: Mining, chopping, farming, fights and finished jobs all pay; building a house pays the most.

entries.title: Come here, stay, and its chunks
q: does my assistant walk to me
assistant stay while i am away
does my assistant keep working when i leave
my assistant stopped working when i went away
how far will my assistant walk
entries.answer: Say "come here" and it makes its way to you on foot, running while it's far and walking the last few blocks, with a word on the distance when it's a long way.
more: It only takes a shortcut when it truly can't get to you for half a minute (and it says so), or when you're in another world.
Told to stay, on guard, at work or walking over to you, it keeps the chunks round it loaded (a 3x3 square), so it really stays put and keeps working while you're hundreds of blocks away.
It lets go of them when it moves on, when it's done, and when it's dismissed or knocked out; normally only while you're online.
Operators set it in Settings, Advanced: on or off, the square's size, the most chunks per player, and whether it carries on while its player is offline.
steps: Say "stay here" where you want it, or give it a job.
Walk off as far as you like: it carries on.
Call it back from anywhere in the same world.
tips: Its Stats tab says when it is keeping chunks loaded, and why.

entries.title: Bedtime for your assistant
q: make my assistant go to bed
entries.answer: At night it sleeps in its bed when you sleep nearby, when you say "go to bed", or (with Shelter at night on) when there's nothing to do.
more: It lies down properly and now and then talks in its sleep.
It gets up in the morning, when you get up, when it's hurt or a monster comes close, or when you say "wake up".
Only players count for skipping the night, so it never holds up your sleep.
Its bed is set with "use this bed" (or by sleeping in one); it comes back there after a fall.
steps: Give it a bed: look at one and say "use this bed".
At night, say "go to bed".
tips: In the day "go to bed" means at dark.

entries.title: Skills and challenges
q: tame a wolf with my assistant
does my assistant fly with me
entries.answer: Say "race me to that tree", "who can mine more in a minute" or "shooting contest" (at a target block); it plays fair at its level and trash-talks within its Language.
more: Trick shots: "shoot that target" (or ping it and pick Trick shot), or "shoot that pig" at something on the move: it aims by the arrow's flight, leads a mover, and says how it went once the arrow lands.
"Tame that wolf" (bones), cats (fish) and parrots (seeds): they're your pets. "Buy bread from that villager" spends the emeralds you give it.
"Brew some healing potions" at a brewing stand, "enchant my sword" at a table (lapis), "upgrade your gear" from its iron and diamonds, "place a lever there", "map this area", "pillar up 5".
"Come to the Nether" and it follows you through; "get 20 quartz from the nether" sends it for some. In the End at level 10 it shoots the crystals, then the dragon.

By itself it raises a shield (4), sprint-jumps gaps of one to three after you (7: short, it pillars out and bridges that gap next time), clutches a long fall with a water bucket (8), puts on an elytra from its pack and glides after you when you fly, with rockets if it has them (8), and pearls to catch up when stuck (9).
A shooting contest is ten shots each; the score shows as it goes.
steps: Look at a tree a fair way off.
Give it the word, then sprint when the countdown ends.
tips: Give it an elytra and a few rockets before you fly: without a rocket it can only take off from somewhere high.
